trust_decision.summary: Whether a domain host is converted to its canonical ASCII (WHATWG/IDNA) form for domainHost schemes is decided only in parseWithStatus from the scheme of the string being parsed; resolve() parses both inputs with scheme 'null', so the merged http/https/ws result is serialized with a raw Unicode host that a WHATWG parser later reads as a different host.

landing_point.why: Summary names scheme-relative references and IDN canonicalization; resolve() is the only function handling relative references and visibly forces scheme 'null' at index.js:28.

fix_sites.entry_point: fastUri.parse / normalize / equal via parseWithStatus (public API, index.js:523-528); refactor into shared canonicalizeHost, no behaviour change (fix.diff:467-515)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Published fix (fix.diff:443-518) only touches resolve() and extracts canonicalizeHost from parseWithStatus, both in index.js; no out-of-scope module changed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: resolveComponent and serialize take already-parsed components, so a solver can argue the caller is responsible for canonicalizing hosts and that only the string resolve() named in the report is affected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Hosts must stay unchanged when unicodeSupport is set or when the effective scheme has no domainHost (e.g. uri://); percent-escaped ASCII reg-names must be kept rather than rejected; mailto keeps its own domain handling (domainHost false, unicodeSupport true). Dropping the scheme:'null' override to get canonicalization would also turn on scheme-specific parse side effects (httpParse 'must have a host' error, wsParse moving path/query into resourceName) for the base and relative inputs.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: index.js:28; index.js:427-429; lib/schemes.js:59-65; lib/schemes.js:89-99; lib/schemes.js:599-612; fix.diff:456-462

O6_input_shapes: scheme-relative reference '//host/...' merged onto an http base (fix.diff:531-534)
Unicode host inherited from the base with a path-only relative reference (fix.diff:537-541)

host that cannot be converted to ASCII must throw, including the scheme-relative, inherited and absolute forms (fix.diff:577-594)

O7_producer.where: index.js:63-122 (resolveComponent builds the merged component; host copied raw at index.js:76, index.js:84, index.js:113)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Public resolveComponent(base, relative, options) returns a merged http component whose host is never canonicalized; with skipNormalization false it re-parses base and relative separately, so a schemeless '//host' relative gets no domainHost handler.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Lower-level component API, documented in types only (types/index.d.ts:41), and README says nothing about it; the report names resolve().
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 15 lines below the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: serialize() of a component with a domainHost scheme writes the host through recomposeAuthority with no IDN canonicalization, so serialize(resolveComponent(...)) or a caller-built component emits the raw Unicode host.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The serializer is meant to emit what it is given; the canonicalization has always lived in the parser, and serialize is a different operation from reference resolution.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: resolveComponent canonicalizing only on its skipNormalization=false branch, so the merged host still skips it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already has a normalize-or-not branch (index.js:66-69) that a maintainer could plausibly reuse for host canonicalization.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: recomposeAuthority un-escaping the host after canonicalization, so a percent-encoded non-ASCII host is decoded after the check has run
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The parser already canonicalizes before un-escaping the host (index.js:426-447), so an ordering differential fits the existing code.
